summary.text: Saffron-clad Oceanid daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, named among the eldest daughters in Hesiod's closing catalogue — a genealogical node with no independent episode in our sources.

story.text: Hesiod closes his register of the chief Oceanids with a cluster of eldest daughters: after Metis and Eurynome come Telesto saffron-clad, Chryseis, Asia, charming Calypso, Eudora, and Tyche — then Amphirho, Ocyrrhoe, and Styx who is chiefest of them all. Telesto shares only this single epithet and list-position; no marriage, no child, no landscape tale attaches to her in the Theogony.

Of the three thousand neat-ankled daughters scattered over earth and sea, Hesiod distinguishes this elder company from the countless remainder — Telesto belongs to the named front rank, not to the silent multitude. The atlas keeps her as a list-node honestly marked: catalogue fact without invented myth.
